notes: Segments of one message are concatenated with nothing between (ABCD), so each segment begins at the next position. Each complete message is one line of DEV.out: the line end is the device's message delimiter, the means by which a variable-length-message device (GR2's 'another computer') tells one message from the next, comparable to the implementor's record delimiter of a variable-length sequential file; it is not a character of any message, and the next message's first character takes the next position available to message data. What a communication device is, and how it frames messages, is the implementor's (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 'Communication devices' documents the device as oriented to variable-length messages, one message per line). Attack point: the reading that DEV.out's bytes are the device's character positions; under it each message after the first starts two positions late (PARTIAL).

next.reason: 1985: "When a receiving communication device ... is oriented to handle variable length messages, each message ... will begin on the next available"; 2023: "No communication devices: 2023 SEND sends a message to a message server run unit (GR-14.9.38.4-4); the communication module is gone". The 2023 SEND belongs to the message-server feature, not the 1985 Communication module. No candidate addresses where variable-length messages are placed on a communication device.
